title: Bluetooth (bluedevil*) crashed in BluezQt::ObexTransfer::transferredChanged when trying to send multiples files to android device
line: Sending several files over Bluetooth no longer crashes after the first file or two.
explanation: obexd reports Status=complete and the final Transferred value in one PropertiesChanged signal. ObexTransferPrivate::propertiesChanged() handles Status first; bluedevil's SendFilesJob reacts to Complete by starting the next file and dropping its only reference to the transfer, which deletes the transfer and its private object while the loop is still running, so the following Transferred emit runs on freed memory. The change (frameworks/bluez-qt!94, applied as is) takes a strong reference to the transfer for the duration of the loop.

commits.message:
ObexTransfer: fix use-after-free when a slot drops the last reference

When Status became Complete, bluedevil moved on to the next file and
dropped the transfer while propertiesChanged() was still looping, so the
Transferred update emitted on freed memory. Hold a strong reference.

BUG: 525109

patches.diff:
From 6639c045da589bfff05782141173861c6ee0eff5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 04:20:09 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] ObexTransfer: fix use-after-free when a slot drops the last
 reference

When Status became Complete, bluedevil moved on to the next file and
dropped the transfer while propertiesChanged() was still looping, so the
Transferred update emitted on freed memory. Hold a strong reference.

BUG: 525109
---
 src/obextransfer.cpp | 9 +++++++++
 1 file changed, 9 insertions(+)

diff --git a/src/obextransfer.cpp b/src/obextransfer.cpp
index 61516cd..6605f50 100644
--- a/src/obextransfer.cpp
+++ b/src/obextransfer.cpp
@@ -74,6 +74,15 @@ void ObexTransferPrivate::propertiesChanged(const QString &interface, const QVar
         return;
     }
 
+    // A slot connected to one of the signals below may drop the last reference
+    // to the transfer (e.g. when it moves on to the next file once the status
+    // becomes Complete). Keep the transfer, and with it this object, alive
+    // until all changed properties have been processed.
+    const ObexTransferPtr guard = q.toStrongRef();
+    if (!guard) {
+        return;
+    }
+
     QVariantMap::const_iterator i;
     for (i = changed.constBegin(); i != changed.constEnd(); ++i) {
         const QVariant &value = i.value();
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Sending 6 files: the transfer stops after the first files and bluedevil-sendfile crashes
Same 6-file send: all files go through and the job finishes
Before: the send job fails with "Application closed unexpectedly"
After: the job keeps going past the point where it crashed (3 of 6), then completes

reviews.text: Clean, minimal fix in the right layer (bluez-qt) for a clear use-after-free in ObexTransferPrivate::propertiesChanged(). Holding a strong ObexTransferPtr guard from q.toStrongRef() for the duration of the loop prevents slots reacting to Status=Complete from freeing the transfer before the batched Transferred update is emitted. The commit message, verification against the reporter's backtrace, media, and passing autotests are all solid and maintainer-ready.

Correct root cause in the right layer: obexd sends Status=complete and Transferred in one PropertiesChanged, QVariantMap iterates Status first, and bluedevil's SendFilesJob drops the last ObexTransferPtr in its statusChanged slot, so the next PROPERTY_CHANGED dereferences freed memory. Holding a strong ref for the loop fixes it for every bluez-qt consumer; deleting the private QObject at the end of its own queued metacall is supported by Qt and nothing touches 'this' after the guard is released. The fake-obexd rig reproduces the reporter's exact backtrace before and completes all 6 files after (video ends with the job gone, no crash notification); commit message matches the diff.
